bug_description.original: Stack-buffer-overflow in se_read_conf OSS-Fuzz report: https://bugs.chromium.org/p/oss-fuzz/issues/detail?id=396958482 ``` Crash type: Stack-buffer-overflow READ 1 Crash state: se_read_conf run_config_handler snmp_config_when ```
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / reproduction_report.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: The staged 151-byte testcase drives `snmp_parse_args_fuzzer` with `argc == 2`. The second 75-byte argv string is the long-option payload `--\t...\tenum\t\xff\xff\xff\xff`, where the payload after `--` contains tabs, the token `enum`, another tab, and four non-ASCII bytes, but no `=` and no literal space. `handle_long_opt()` therefore copies that payload and appends the synthetic suffix `" 1"`, creating a remembered config line whose first token is `enum` and whose argument string is `\xff\xff\xff\xff 1`. During `init_snmp()`, `read_configs()` replays remembered config lines; `snmp_config_when()` tokenizes this line on spaces, tabs, and `=`, finds the registered `enum` handler, and calls `se_read_conf()` with the remainder `\xff\xff\xff\xff 1`. `se_read_conf()` copies the first remainder token into `e_name`, takes the named-enumeration branch because `e_name` is not `major:minor`, then copies the next token into the stack buffer `e_enum`, yielding the short string `"1"`. The check `sscanf(e_enum, "%d:", &value) != 1` treats `"1"` as a successful numeric prefix even though there is no colon, and the vulnerable loop `while (*(cp2++) != ':')` then scans for `:` without checking for the terminating NUL first. Because `e_enum` contains no colon, that loop reads past the end of the fixed `e_enum[BUFSIZ]` stack buffer until AddressSanitizer reports the saved stack-buffer-overflow read at `snmplib/snmp_enum.c:153`. The patch adds the missing `*cp2` bound check to stop at the NUL terminator before scanning into the redzone.

source.description: First project statement on the crashing path that materializes attacker-controlled bytes into a config-line buffer later replayed by the config parser.
source.value_from: The staged PoC is `gt_results/osv_ossfuzz_OSV-2025-133/poc` (151 bytes, SHA-256 `bcf3dc035d213734cb5801d7d952979507e817cd8b34c8dec49e4727fc6aaabb`). Byte 0 is `0x01`, so the harness computes `argc == 2`. The second 75-byte argv string is `--\t...\tenum\t\xff\xff\xff\xff\0`, so `getopt()` reaches `case '-'` and passes the payload after `--` into `handle_long_opt()`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: Because the attacker payload contains no `=` and no literal space, `handle_long_opt()` synthesizes the trailing token `1`. That synthetic token is later copied into `e_enum` and scanned for a nonexistent colon.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The colon-scan loop checks only for `':'` and does not stop when `cp2` reaches the terminating NUL of `e_enum`, so a token like `"1"` makes the scan walk off the fixed stack buffer.
root_cause.note: The staged patch changes this loop to `while (*cp2 && *(cp2++) != ':')`, making NUL termination an explicit bound check before advancing.

sink.description: ASan crash site. This loop performs the out-of-bounds read when it dereferences past the end of `e_enum` while searching for a colon that is not present.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow` with frame `se_read_conf /gt/_work/src/snmplib/snmp_enum.c:153:20`, and the frame layout marks `e_enum` as the overflown stack object.

parser_admitted.description: After tokenization on spaces, tabs, and `=`, the remembered line's first token is `enum`, so handler lookup finds the registered enum config parser instead of rejecting the line as an unknown token.

fine_trace.note: Source. The long-option helper copies the attacker-controlled payload after `--` into a mutable config buffer. For the staged witness that payload is tabs, the token `enum`, another tab, and four `0xff` bytes.

Because the copied payload contains no `=` and no literal space character, this helper takes its fallback path and appends `" 1"`. The resulting config text is `\t...\tenum\t\xff\xff\xff\xff 1`, which creates the later standalone numeric token `1`.
The synthetic config line from step 2 is duplicated into the config memory list, preserving it for deferred processing during `init_snmp()`.

When `read_configs()` replays remembered config lines, it feeds the stored attacker-controlled line back into the config parser. This is the order edge that reconnects the deferred config text to the vulnerable parser path.

The config parser tokenizes the remembered line on spaces, tabs, and `=`. This skips the leading tabs and extracts `enum` as the directive token, selecting the enum configuration path for the same attacker-controlled line.

Handler lookup finds the config handler registered as `register_const_config_handler(type, "enum", se_read_conf, NULL, NULL)`, so `run_config_handler()` invokes `se_read_conf()` with `token == "enum"` and the remaining argument string `\xff\xff\xff\xff 1`.

Inside `se_read_conf()`, the first remaining token is copied into `e_name` as the four-byte string `\xff\xff\xff\xff`. That string does not match `major:minor`, so execution falls through to the named-enumeration branch.

The next token in the named-enumeration branch is copied into the fixed stack buffer `e_enum`. Because step 2 appended `" 1"`, this copy materializes the short NUL-terminated string `"1"` in `e_enum`.

This check only requires `%d` to assign successfully. For `e_enum == "1"`, `sscanf` stores `value == 1` and returns 1 even though no colon follows, so the parser continues on a token that has a numeric prefix but no separator.

Root cause step. `cp2` starts at `e_enum`, but this loop checks only for `':'` and not for the terminating NUL. With `e_enum == "1"`, it reads the `'1'`, then the NUL, then keeps advancing through the rest of the stack buffer looking for a colon that does not exist.

Sink step. Because step 10 never stops at the NUL terminator, the same loop eventually dereferences one byte beyond `e_enum[BUFSIZ]` and ASan reports a stack-buffer-overflow read on the `e_enum` stack object at line 153.

format.name: snmp_parse_args_fuzzer fixed-width argv encoding
format.contract: The witness is exactly 151 bytes: byte 0 must make `(af_get_short(&data, &size) % 99) + 1 == 2`, so the harness reads exactly two 75-byte argv strings. The second 75-byte string must begin with `--`, contain only tab separators before the directive token `enum`, then a tab and four nonzero bytes, and must contain neither `=` nor a literal space before its terminating NUL. Under `handle_long_opt()`, that exact shape forces the helper to append `" 1"`, so the remembered config line later reaches `se_read_conf()` with a named-enum list name followed by the standalone numeric token `1` that lacks the required colon.
